Subject: Sudden p95 jump & 503s after on-prem agent update

Jonas / Marissa —

We pushed the agent 2.3.1 to our on-prem cluster last night and since ~02:30 UTC we've observed a sustained p95 latency jump from ~180ms to ~1.2s and a 5xx spike (~12% of requests returning 503) across several nodes. Throughput visible to us dropped by ~30%.

Attached is a short log excerpt (edge_error_log_excerpt.txt) and a KV cache snapshot we pulled (kv_cache_snapshot.json). The stack traces show repeated "KV cache miss + fallback decode" patterns and some RPC timeout messages to the local runtime.

This is customer-impacting — our CEO (Megan) is asking for immediate remediation and an exec-level update. Please advise next steps and an ETA for rollback or mitigation.

Thanks,
Alan
Site Reliability Lead
EdgePlatform

Quick triage notes (prelim):
- Symptoms line up with a kernel-ABI mismatch introduced in agent 2.3.1 that changes the pinned fused-kernel selector for fused attention. On certain NVIDIA driver combos this forces a slower execution path and higher lock contention for the KV cache.
- The runtime falls back on an emulation path causing increased CPU work per token and occasional timeouts to local RPCs (hence 503s).

Immediate remediation (recommended):
1) Roll back agent to 2.3.0 on the affected nodes (fastest path).
2) If rollback not possible, switch runtime kernel selector to "compat-mode" (safe) — this reduces throughput but restores tail latency.
3) Collect a full kernel trace and current /proc/cmdline from all affected nodes (I requested an expanded log bundle; see JIRA OPS-4821).

I can lead the rollback. Estimated timeline:
- Rollback prep + change window (30–45m)
- Rollback execution (rolling, 10–15m per node depending on cluster size)
- Post-rollback verification (20–30m)

Attaching a short checklist: prelim_kernel_checks.md (internal).

-Markus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
